_comment: Hierarchical AllGather on the same 96-GPU dual-plane cluster, SCATTERED placement: GPU g -> leaf (g % 3), so each host straddles all three leaves 6/5/5 (16-GPU hosts) or 2/3/3 (8-GPU hosts). A/B partner of dual_plane_clustered_hierarchical_allgather.json. Note the coarse graph differs structurally: each host has SIX thin uplinks (250-300 GB/s) instead of TWO fat ones (800 GB/s), which gives the coarse LP more routing freedom.
_expected: Host-uplink bound T* >= 0.880 s = 44 epochs, set by the 8-GPU hosts (704 GB across the host boundary / 800 GB/s of dual-plane egress). The spine cut is SLACK at 0.640 s, which is the whole point of a non-blocking fabric -- so LATENCY SHOULD TIE between clustered and scattered. The comparison lives in objective_type 5's switch-hop tie-breaker term: scattered puts 33.3% of cross-host GPU pairs on a shared leaf vs clustered's 22.6%, so scattered should show strictly FEWER leaf->spine hops at the same makespan. A latency DIFFERENCE means something is wrong (or an uplink got tapered).
_epoch_note: epoch_duration is PINNED to 0.02 s (= 1/50 GB/s, the fine GPU->leaf link) rather than derived, and this is load-bearing for the A/B. Derived SLOWEST_LINK sizing would give the two placements DIFFERENT epochs -- SLOWEST_LINK reads the MIN coarse capacity, which is 400 GB/s clustered vs 100 GB/s scattered -- a 4x difference in quantum, giving 0.0025 s vs 0.0100 s -- so the makespans would differ by epoch quantization rather than by placement quality. Same epoch on both sides is what makes the comparison mean anything.
_known_failure: The coarse LP can trip account_for_consume's 'assert consume == 0' on sub-feasibility-tol Gurobi flow noise (see the lp_extraction_feasibility_tol_noise note). feasibility_tol is tightened to 1e-6 here to make that less likely; if it still fires, that is the known extraction bug, not a topology problem.
_max_denom_note: KNOWN FAILURE, not fixable by raising max_denom further -- this is coarse-LP/proportional-split degeneracy (see the coarse_lp_degeneracy_symmetry_enforcement / coarse_lp_objective_regularization memory notes), not a bounded precision gap. Traced 2026-08-24 by replaying the logged coarse solve (Schedules/dual_plane_scattered_alltoall_coarse.json) through identity_sets/_build_slots/_solve_assignment directly (deterministic, no Gurobi needed): identity (0,17) -> cell 1's full 4-piece group is EXACTLY {1/6, 277/1250, 232/1875, 61/125} (each machine-precision exact, verified by decoding, not approximated), whose LCM is 3750 -- not a small denominator, a real one, from the scattered placement's uneven 6/5/5 GPUs-per-leaf split compounding a factor of 5 at each of several proportional-split stages (_build_slots then _solve_assignment). max_denom and feasibility_tol are coupled (grid_resolution = 1/(2*max_denom^2) must exceed feasibility_tol): at this file's feasibility_tol=1e-6, max_denom must stay < 707, which cannot reach 3750, and there is no guarantee 3750 is even the worst case elsewhere in the schedule. max_denom=128 below is left in place (harmless, and it does fix the SIMPLER dual_plane_clustered_hierarchical_alltoall.json-style cases) but this specific input needs the coarse-LP symmetry/regularization fix, not another max_denom bump. Do NOT copy max_denom=128 onto an input using the default feasibility_tol=1e-4 -- that pairing is illegal at MAX_DENOM=128 (snap_tolerance raises at construction).
_topology_note: The topology comes from the .topo DSL file (teccl/topologies/topology-dsl-frontend/examples/dual_plane_hetero_scattered.topo), not from the hand-written DualPlaneHeteroClusterScattered class: topo_file SELECTS the topology, so TECCLSolver.get_topology builds a DslTopology from it and `name` is left as the free-form label the output filenames and Gurobi log are built from. The file is a verified port of the class -- same 114 node indices, same capacities, same ports/port order, same radix, same symmetry groups, same 8 cells -- so this input solves the same problem it did before, and the placement rule now lives in the .topo file rather than in DualPlaneHeteroClusterScattered._gpu_leaf. The path is relative to the repo root, i.e. to the directory `teccl solve` runs from.
